title: Negative redshift making it through LCFIT
body:
I have an LCFIT job that runs successfully but later causes errors when running BBC because there are SNe somehow making it through with zHEL=0 (negative for zCMB). This is only a problem when I am running LCFIT+z. I'm not sure a) how negative redshifts aren't getting cut and b) how they are fitted with z=0 to begin with.

Directory is /scratch/midway2/rkessler/PIPPIN_OUTPUT/RC_DESPZ_MASTER/2_LCFIT/DATAFIT_DATADES/output
Examples of z=0 SNe:
SN: 1259541 in FITOPT001 (OPT_PHOTOZ=4, use zphot quantiles)
SN: 1308074 in FITOPT002,4,5 (OPT_PHOTOZ=1, use gaussian photoz host prior)

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
the sim has no protection against blue-shifts (which are rare, but possible) and it is up to the user to set parameters to avoid this. A simulated blue shift can happen from helio->CMB transformation or from Vpec. In LC fit stage, have you tried
   CUTWIN_REDSHIFT = 0.005, 2.0

comments.author: rebeccachen0
comments.body: I do have CUTWIN_REDSHIFT  =  0.05, 1.2 in the LC fit nml. This is also with data, and I am using header override files for the host galaxy photo-z (which is not zero)

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: This event has z_spec = 0.9 so it passes CUTWIN_REDHIFT. The issue is that the photo-z estimate is very far off resulting in crazy fitted zphot. Will need to investigate this fit more carefully and hopefully find a robust way to reject it.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
FITPROB = 1.335460e-22 for this event, so just change
FITWIN_PROB = 0.0,  1.01
  to
FITWIN_PROB = 0.01,  1.01

comments.author: rebeccachen0
comments.body: SN 1308074 in FITOPTs 2,4,5 also has fitted redshift of 0 with FITPROB 7.82426e-02 so a FITPROB cut is not sufficient

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
There are two problems with the LC-fit inputs. First, the header override file defined
    HOSTGAL_ZPHOT   HOSTGAL_ZPHOTERR
instead of
   HOSTGAL_PHOTOZ  HOSTGAL_PHOTOZ_ERR
Unfortunately the SNANA codes use a mix of ZPHOT and PHOTOZ conventions, so I added a "mistaken varname" code trap for the override file that will abort and indicate the correct varname to use. 

For FITOPT002 with OPT_PHOTOZ=1, the 2nd problem is that PRIOR_ZERRSCALE was not specified and thus the default value of 1000 essentially made the host photo-z prior a flat prior. Setting PRIOR_ZERRSCALE=1 results in reasonable output for SNID= 1308074

comments.author: rebeccachen0
comments.body: It's odd that the default is PRIOR_ZERRSCALE=1000 as I hadn't explicitly set it to 1 in these other sim fits (/scratch/midway2/rkessler/PIPPIN_OUTPUT/RC_DESPZ_MASTER/2_LCFIT/DFIT_DES_P21), but the fitted photo-z are different for each fitopt (which have different host priors) ?

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: PRIOR_ZERRSCALE likely does not impact quantiles, but it does impact using photo-z mean and STD as prior.

comments.author: rebeccachen0
comments.body: Setting PRIOR_ZERRSCALE=1.0 still results in fitted z=0 for e.g. 1304045 in FITOPT004

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: for SNID= 1304045, the real zSpec = 0.8, so with photo-z ~ 0 the fitted stretch x1=4.6 is way outside the nominal bound of |x1| < 3

comments.author: rebeccachen0
comments.body: How is it possible that the best fit photo-z is 0 though? The host priors are ~0.3, 0.15 for DNF, BPZ respectively, so it's unclear how the chi2 would be favored at z=0

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: the host photo-z ~ .2 is very far away from the true zSpec ~ 0.8, so it's not clear how the photo-z fit behaves in such a pathological situation. The real stretch is multiplied by 1+z = 1.8 for the observer frame, and with photo-z ~ 0 the fitted stretch absorbs 1+zSpec and is thus unphysical.

comments.author: rebeccachen0
comments.body: Okay, any recommendation for how to cut these kinds of pathological fits? Just raising the minimum FITPROB?

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: A combination of cuts on FITPROB, color, stretch will hopefully remove pathological fits. Rather than identifying one event at a time, can you analyze a large sample and try to find ~dozen(s) of them?

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: closing issue for now; re-open as needed.

comments.author: anaismoller
comments.body:
HNY!

I have shipped a bug fix and deployed it in midway. As you suspected, it was the change in filter names. Specifically, you are trying to use a model trained with simulations using g r i z filters and applying it to simulations with DES-g DES-r DES-i DES-z filters. 

In an ideal world I would suggest retraining the models to avoid a patch that is not robust. But we don't want to reproduce the models/simulations used in the DES 5-yr analysis. So, I have fixed this ONLY for DES backward compatibility in the `SuperNNova` branch `SNANA_DES5yr`. It is deployed in midway already so just relaunch your jobs.

Of course, if the results seem weird, don't hesitate to ping me, I tried to check the best I could but you never know! An example of one I ran is in:

comments.author: anaismoller
comments.body:
You are trying to build a database with filters: DES-g, DES-r, etc but the simulations only have a filter column with g,r, etc. So for the database you need to use `--list_filters g i r z`. I think this is something that can be tuned with PIPPIN @OmegaLambda1998 ? I can put a more explicit error in the output but recognising automatically the filters within SNN can be a source of additional issues...

The bug I fixed in this issue is that you can use a model trained with DES-g, DES-r on data created with g r ... 

I created a `job_AM.slurm` in the same folder that has the correct syntax.

Does this make sense?

comments.body:
```
opts:
    LIST_FILTERS: ["g", "r", "i", "z"]
```

Defaults to `["DES-g", "DES-r", "DES-i", "DES-z"]` following some recent changes

fill_TABLE_MWXT_SEDMODEL() is called from genmag_SALT2, but here the first event (z=5.1) has no bands within SALT2 model range and thus fill_TABLE_MWXT_SEDMODEL() is not called. But then genSpec_SALT2 is called and tries using the MWXT table that has not been allocated or filled.

Fix is to call fill_TABLE_MWXT_SEDMODEL() from genSpec_SALT2 ... it does nothing if already called from genmag_SALT2.

title: Rethinking pz systematic common event logic
body:
When definition of nominal sample is dependent on having a "good" pz estimate, fitopts which use other estimates may be missing information for events in the nominal sample. One option is to reject the event and continue rather than aborting on "no quantiles" error.

Example:
CID=250945 host 2200135032
Host 2200135032 has pz in $DES_USERS/rebeccachen/inputs_pippin_D5YR_PASTRY/base_files/overrides/des_sim_header_override_knn_refmt.txt but not in $DES_USERS/rebeccachen/inputs_pippin_D5YR_PASTRY/base_files/overrides/des_sim_header_override_bpz_refmt.txt

FITOPT001 is to override with BPZ and fails with "  - zPDF quantiles requested for photo-z fit to CID=250945

The GENPDF file used to generate the sims is `/project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/ATLAS/USERS/jtweddle/BIASCOR/PIPPIN_FILES/SIM_BIASCOR.input`, and contains the following:

GENPEAK_SALT2BETA: 2.64601

GENRANGE_SALT2BETA: 2.5 2.8
```

This appears to be a similar issue to that raised here: https://github.com/RickKessler/SNANA/issues/808
and it seems like this is an issue that has cropped up before as I was looking at the previous GENPDF file I was using (`$SNDATA_ROOT/models/population_pdf/DES-SN5YR/DES-SN5YR_DES_S3_P21.DAT`), which contains the following:

For the q000 issue, the first event (SNID= 11934165 ) has the following HOSTLIB information:
GALID  = 7937500077
ZTRUE  = 0.05045
ZPHOT  = 2.95926
ZPHOT_Q000  ZPHOT_Q010  ZPHOT_Q020 =  -9.0     2.92666     2.93481

The photo-z estimate here is clearly catastrophic and the photo-z quantile code returned -9 in the zero-prob quantile bin. The true SN redshift for this event is 0.07041, and it picked host ZTRUE=0.05045 as within redshift tolerance of  0.02  + 0.01*z +  0.007*z^2.
To match the SN redshift, the quantile redshifts are all scaled by 0.07041/0.05045 = 1.396, and the -9 value that means NULL is scaled to the bizarre value of -12.56.

A proper fix would be in the quantile-generation code, but here I fixed the SNANA simulation to preserved the -9 value so that it can be clearly interpreted as NULL. Each broker will need to figure out how to handle this situation for ELASTICC, and hopefully there will be an upstream PZ fix before commissioning.

The fix is in function GEN_SNHOST_ZPHOT_QUANTILE (sntools_host.c),

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: I have fixed the sim to give a proper abort message (see attachment). The issue is that the spectrograph wave range goes just outside the primary SED range, where the primary is defined in kcor file. Another subtle issue is that the spectrograph wave range is internally extended (based on wave resolution) in order to properly account for wave-smearing near the edges. In your sim job, it adds one more wave bin, which brings the range just outside the 12600 A range of the primary SED. The simple fix is to trim the spectrograph wave range by few tens of A, and remake the kcor-input file.

title: Unable to simulate UV spectra with snlc_sim

I was trying to simulated some SNe Ia sample with UV spectra (wavelngth range ~ 1800-10000A) with snlc_sim.exe. However, the minimum wavelength of output spectra only goes down to 3600A. Is there a way to simulate the UV spectra?

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: There are two issues with your spectra being truncated. First, when using TAKE_SPECTRUM keys in the SIMLIB file, the output spectrum is constrained to be within the wavelengths provided in the SNR_LAMOBS key. The reasoning is that the sim should only generate within the wave range of the actual data that these TAKE_SPECTRUM keys represent. It doesn't make sense to simulate & analyze spectra that extend in wavelength beyond actual data. Beyond the first issue, there is additional wavelength truncation due to invalid ZP_SPECTROGRAPH calculation (see manual screen shot below). The current sim code rejects wave bins with ZP<0 (i.e., "invalid"), but does not give any warning, which can result in wave bins mysteriously not appearing in the output spectra. For your spectrograph, about 1/3 of the wave bins have invalid ZP_SPECTROGRAPH < 0, and this is because of the values in MAGREF_LIST: 17.0 32.0 The bright end of 17 is fine, but the faint end of 32 is far too faint, resulting in a poor estimate of ZP. Would suggest increasing the faint end to be closer to the faint end of SN that pass your selection criteria. To avoid future confusion, I added a diagnostic to print ZP(min, max) and to abort if more than 2% of the wave bins fail the ZP>0 cut. Your test job now aborts with this error: FATAL ERROR ABORT called by INIT_SPECTROGRAPH_SEDMODEL Invalid ZP_SPECTROGRAPH frac = 0.335; exceeds FRAC_ZP_INVALID_ABORT=0.020 Check MAGREF_LIST in spectrograph table I checked this diagnostic on the Roman PRISM, and ZPmin/max is about 10-11, well above the ZP>0 requirement. If this 2% abort threshold is too severe, I can loosen it or add another sim-input key allowing user-defined threshold, but was hoping to avoid yet another input key.

title: release refactor to add HOSTGALz_XXX (HOSTGAL2z_XXX) vectors to data structure
body:
The original photo-z quantile structure in SNANA data files was to have explicit 
ZPHOT_Q000, ZPHOT_Q010, ZPHOT_Q020 ... ZPHOT_Q100 
columns, and the quantile percentiles were fixed. This rigid structure allowed only 11 quantiles, and worked only for the nearest host. This data structure needs to be more flexible for quantiles, and to allow a new LOGMASS grid so that LOGMASS can be evaluated after the SN+HOST lightcurve fit.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
New data stream vectors are

TTYPE62 = 'HOSTGALz_NBIN_QUANTILE_ZPHOT' / label for field  62                  
TTYPE63 = 'HOSTGALz_QUANTILE_ZPHOT' / label for field  63                       
TTYPE64 = 'HOSTGALz_QUANTILE_PERCENT' / label for field  64      
               
TTYPE65 = 'HOSTGALz_NBIN_LOGMASS_ZGRID' / label for field  65                   
TTYPE66 = 'HOSTGALz_LOGMASS_ZGRID' / label for field  66                        
TTYPE67 = 'HOSTGALz_LOGMASS_VALGRID' / label for field  67                      
TTYPE68 = 'HOSTGALz_LOGMASS_ERRGRID' / label for field  68     

TTYPE105= 'HOSTGAL2z_NBIN_QUANTILE_ZPHOT' / label for field 105                 
TTYPE106= 'HOSTGAL2z_QUANTILE_ZPHOT' / label for field 106                      
TTYPE107= 'HOSTGAL2z_QUANTILE_PERCENT' / label for field 107       
             
TTYPE108= 'HOSTGAL2z_NBIN_LOGMASS_ZGRID' / label for field 108                  
TTYPE109= 'HOSTGAL2z_LOGMASS_ZGRID' / label for field 109                       
TTYPE110= 'HOSTGAL2z_LOGMASS_VALGRID' / label for field 110                     
TTYPE111= 'HOSTGAL2z_LOGMASS_ERRGRID' / label for field 111

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: there is a new caveat reading these vectors with python. While reading FITS data into astropy table works fine, table.to_pandas() fails on the vector columns, which caused scone to fail. The scone fix in $SCONE_DIR/create_heatmaps/helpers.py was to add a new function, remove_vector_columns(table), that removes vector columns before converting to pandas. Perhaps a more simple one-liner can be identified later.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
LEGACY COLUMN NAMES: 

for the HOSTLIB read by simulation, the legacy columns HOSTGAL_ZPHOT_Q000 ... HOSTGAL_ZPHOT_Q100 are still allowed, but recommend replacing with the more flexible QZPHOT00 ... QZPHOTnn column names.

OVERRIDE files (read by snana.exe and snlc_fit.exe)  IMPLICIT z-list must use QZPHOT00, QZPHOT01 ... QZPHOTnn, where PERCENTILES are computed with implicit assumption about equal-spaced quantile probs. If legacy HOSTGAL_ZPHOT_Qnn are detected, the code aborts with instructions to use the QZPHOT column names.

In short, old notation still allowed for HOSTLIB_FILE, but not for HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: OPT_PHOTOZ += 32768 (internally convert Gauss PDF into quantiles) is broken, and needs to be fixed later (or removed). Follow USE_QGAUSS logical in sntools_host.c. This is a feature only for debugging, so not critical.

title: Excess of SNe Ia in LSST simulation
body:
Hi,

Running a Rubin-LSST simulation on NERSC with @erikpeterson23  we found an excess of generated supernovae.
We are simulating 10 years of Rubin-LSST with two different simulations for "low-z" (0 <  z < 0.11) and "high-z" (0.11 < z < 1.3). For the high-z sample, we are finding, after fit cuts, ~ 1.5 million SNe Ia, which seems overestimated.

The cadence file is : `$SNANA_LSST_ROOT/simlibs/baseline_v4.3_10yrs_all.SIMLIB.COADD`
With survey parameters:
```
SOLID_ANGLE: 6.225
TOTAL_AREA: 20434.964
DNDZ: POWERLAW 2.06E-5 1.7 # Frohmaier 2019 rescale to h = 0.6774
```
The simulation is distributed over 10 CPUs using:

```
    NGEN_UNIT: 0.1
    RANSEED_REPEAT: 10 17234
    BATCH_INFO: sbatch $SBATCH_TEMPLATES/SBATCH_DEFAULT.TEMPLATE 20
```

We are applying SEARCHEFF detection cut using:
```
SEARCHEFF_PIPELINE_EFF_FILE: $SNANA_LSST_ROOT/models/searcheff/SEARCHEFF_PIPELINE_LSST_DC2_Run2.2i_WFD.DAT
SEARCHEFF_PIPELINE_LOGIC_FILE: $SNANA_LSST_ROOT/models/searcheff/SEARCHEFF_PIPELINE_LOGIC_DC2_Run2.2i_WFD.DAT
```

The overall PIPPIN configuration is given in: `$PIPPIN_OUTPUT/EP-LSST/EP-LSST.yml`

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
From Phil Gris work, we expect about 20,000 SNIa after cuts in DDF (e.g., see Fig 1 in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.10781) that spans 50 deg sq. Guessing that the WFD will have 1/5 the number of SN per sq deg results in 4,000 per 50 deg sq. Over half the sky we naively expect
   N(WFD) ~ 20,000(DDF) * (1/5) * (20,000/50) = 1.6 million
which is pretty close to what you find above.

comments.author: bastiencarreres
comments.body:
In [Gris et al. 2023](https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/1538-4365/ac9e58/pdf) it is stated:

> In a recent paper (Lochner et al. 2022), the LSST Dark
Energy Science Collaboration (DESC) has presented an
analysis from the WFD survey observing strategies simulated
by the LSST project. 12 The conclusion is that an unprecedented
number of well-measured SNe Ia will be observed in the WFD
survey (between 120,000 and 170,000) up to redshifts z ∼ 0.3.

Do you think there is an error in this statement? or am I mis-understanding something?

comments.author: bastiencarreres
comments.body: Also DDF is going deeper: if we said that DDF is complete up to `z~1.1` and WFD is complete up to `z~0.5` it gives an extra 0.15 factor in term of volume ratio. Thus the volume of WFD is N(WFD) = 20,000(DDF) * (1/5) * (20,000/50)  * 0.15  ~  240 000 SNe Ia

title: Develop REWGT mechanism for biasCor sims
body:
BBC always rejects a small fraction of events due to insufficient sim stats in regions of large stretch and/or color. A larger fraction of events that are kept have biasCor errors that are difficult to quantify. To better sample sparsely populated x1,c regions, biasCor sim should generated using
   PROB(population) -> PROB^ PROB_EXPON_REWGT
where PROB_EXPON_REWGT is a user-input. 

PROB_EXPON_REWGT=1 --> does nothing new; same as before

PROB_EXPON_REWGT = 0  -->  flat distribution, 
PROB_EXPON_REWGT = 0.5 ->  in PROB -> SQRT(PROB) and thus a 1% prob region becomes 10% and gets x10 more stats. 
The resulting weight factor,
    WGT_POP = Product_{color, stretch} PROB^{1-PROB_EXPON_REWGT}
needs to be included in the sim-output and propagated to SALT2mu/BBC so that appropriate weighted biasCor is computed

This update involves changes to simulation and to SALT2mu/BBC codes.

  final_cov = cov.copy()

2)
effective_cov=cov_sys + np.diag(base[VARNAME_MUERR]**2) # <-- core dump

  diag_muerr_cov = np.diag(base[VARNAME_MUERR]**2))

error = np.linalg.norm(np.eye(n) - 
                     matrix.dot( matrix.transpose().conjugate()))  # <-- core dump
replaced with:
    tmp1 = np.eye(n)
    tmp2 = matrix.dot( matrix.transpose().conjugate())
    tmpdif = tmp1 - tmp2
    error  = np.linalg.norm(tmpdif)

title: with SIMLIB_OUT option, write TAKE_SPECTRUM keys in SIMLIB header
body: using SIMLIB_OUT option with snana.exe, if there are spectra in the data then include a TAKE_SPECTRUM key in the SIMLIB header for each spectrum. This feature is useful to test training by enabling simulating spectra with the same phase and SNR as in the data.

comments.author: djones1040
comments.body:
I set up the `$SNANA_DEBUG/djones/specsim` for this.  All of the namelist files in that directory should work for creating SIMLIB files:
```
snana.exe snfit_Hamuy1996.nml SIMLIB_OUT Hamuy86.SIMLIB
```
The SURVEY keys in the LC files don't match up with `$SNDATA_ROOT/SURVEY.DEF` though.  On my local machine I just added these surveys to SURVEY.DEF but that's probably not the best.

comments.author: RickKessler

comments.author: djones1040
comments.body:
running some tests and found that SNR computation is very sensitive to outliers.  Check out `$SNANA_DEBUG/djones/specsim4`.  If you run the command:
```
snana.exe snfit_SNLS3_test.nml SIMLIB_OUT SNLS3_TEST.SIMLIB
```
you'll see two SIMLIB entries from the same SN.  one has a TAKE_SPECTRUM line with SNR of 0.1, one has a TAKE_SPECTRUM line with SNR of 553.  The difference between the two is that I've masked out a few data points with crazy high errors in the second LC file.  These regions were data quality = 0 so they should have been masked anyways.  But this issue might pop back up if there are regions with sky lines or something that have crazy high errors.

title: Numerical issue when MUERR is < E-3
body:
Working with Rick on simulating LSST, and while chasing down a bias, Rick noticed that in a regions of my Hubble diagram, MUERR (stat-only) reached below 10^-3. When we then tested if this could be relevant to the bias we were seeing, we included an -snrms option at the wfit stage, e.g.,

```
wfit.exe FITOPT000_MUOPT001.M0DIF.gz -speed_flag_chi2 2 -w0min -2 -w0max 0 -w0steps 1201 -ommin 0.0 -ommax 1.0 -omsteps 601 \
    -snrms 0.002 \
    -outfile_cospar out_wfit_snrms002.cospar \
    >& out_wfit_snrms002.log &
```
and we observed that the bias went away (this can be reproduced in `$SNANA_DEBUG/wfit_snrms` on nersc by running `./run_wfit_ep_lsst.sh`). 

Initially w was equal to -0.938 +/- 0.008. 

- With -snrms of 0.001, w is -0.975 +/- 0.013. 
- For -snrms of 0.002, w goes to -0.988 +/- 0.020. 
- And when -snrms at 0.004 w goes to -0.993 +/- 0.032.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
For above wfit tests, -snrms was used for stat-only mode without a covariance matrix, but I noticed that -snrms is ignored when reading a cov matrix.  I fixed wfit to apply -snrms to MUCOV when reading MUCOV_SYS, and to abort when reading MUCOV_TOT_INV since there is no easy way to update the already-inverted cov matrix.


By default, MUCOV_TOT_INV is written in 7_CREATE_COV stage of pippin, so adding -snrms option to wfit (stage 8 of pippin) will result in abort. To use -snrms with pippin, define
   EXTRA_OPTS:  --write_mask_cov 1
under the 7_CREATE_COV block in pippin-input file, which will write COVSYS matrix, instead of the fully-inverted matrix. The COSMOFIT task of submit_batch_jobs (run by pippin) should figure out which cov matrix exists.

The underlying problem is that the SPEC and zHOST map codes are mostly independent and they do not share attributes. For example SPEC_FILE map can define colors, but zHOST cannot; zHOST map can use only HOSTLIB variables while SPEC map canot use HOSTLIB variables.

The fix requires a semi-major refactor in two parts:
1. in sntools_trigger.c[h],  merge SPEC and zHOST-map code into a single code operating on a well defined SEARCHEFF_MAP_DEF object, and 
2. in sntools_host.c[h], read HOSTLIB variables before checking SPEC,zHOST,GENPDF map variables; split old read_head_HOSTLIB() into two parts, read_head_HOSTLIB and prep_head_HOSTLIB().

comments.body: I look at few LC of cutted SN Ia but didn't notice something special. Here is an example: The vertical line represent the estimated PEAKMJD from snlc_fit.exe

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
The paradox is due to different definitions of CUTWIN_TRESTMIN[MAX] in the sim and in the analysis code (likely an accident  in the distant past). The simulation cut is on any epoch, but the snlc_fit analysis cut is on the extreme min or max within CUTWIN_TREST. With your current cuts,

 CUTWIN_TREST     = -20.0,   60.0
  cutwin_Trestmin  = -10.0   0.
   cutwin_Trestmax  =  0.   30.

if there is an observation with TREST between -20 and -10, it will fail the cut. Similarly, a TREST observation between 30 and 60 fails cut. The intended usage here is
cutwin_Trestmin  = -20.0   0
cutwin_Trestmax  =  0.   60.

which recovers all the events.
I would recommend NOT using CUTWIN in the simulation because it does not always map into analysis cuts. Sim CUTS use truth, for example, not measured values. I have even thought about removing the CUTWIN feature in the sim.

To do what you want, we could add something like
    SNCUT_NOBS_TREST = '1 -10 0 : 2 0 30'
meaning at least 1 obs from -10 to 0, and at least 2 obs from 0 to 30.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
this is a subtle gzip bug that I have never been able to fix. When reading a gzip file, rewind causes a rare corruption and thus rewind is not used for gzip files. Even closing and re-opening the gzip file can cause corruption. For GENPDF_FILE, the snana_open command searches for DOCUMENTATION block on first line, but doesn't find it because VARNAMES is on the first line in this particular gzipped GENPDF_FILE. Without the rewind, the remainder of the read-code does not find the first VARNAMES that was already ready while looking for the DOCUMENTATION key.

The simple solution here is to gunzip the GENPDF_FILE (which I did), and the code goes past the previous abort. A more robust solution is to add a DOCUMENTATION block at the top of the file.

The test.cmd job still aborts with a different error:

 FATAL ERROR ABORT called by ENDSIMLIB_check
   Could not find SIMLIB HEADER passing GENRANGE_XXX cuts.
   Check USE_SIMLIB_XXX flags and header values.

This is a rather subtle feature that can be avoided. When using submit_batch_jobs.py, the default behavior is to suppress model-specific parameters. The reason is to avoid confusion in the analysis when reading data files in which model parameters suddenly change because GENMODEL changes. This suppression is done by automatically adding command line override
WRFLAG_MODELPAR:  0

To undo this flag, add 
WRFLAG_MODELPAR : 1
under the GENOPT_GLOBAL block as illustrated in
$SNANA_LSST_USERS/smithmat/tides_sims/inputs/RICK_SIMGEN_MASTER.INPUT

Next, make sure to remove "SIMGEN_DUMPADD: stretch,color" because stretch  & color are automatically added to SIMGEN_DUMP, and requesting them explicitly results in abort on duplicate SIMGEN_DUMP variables.

The problem is that Gauss sigma = 0.01 is <<< BETA range between peak and edges of range. The course-grid search of PROB fails to find prob>0 because it skips over the effective delta-function.

The fix in init_genPDF_from_GenGauss() is to modify RANGE to be within 8 sigma of peak. A warning about the change is printed to stdout, but the user need not know about it.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
This fix was tricky because data files don't contain quantiles and thus the default override procedure doesn't even check the quantiles. Even if the data includes quantiles, the number of override quantiles could be different than the original. I therefore added a new rd_override_zphot_q() function (in sntools_data.c) that always forces an override regardless of whether quantiles exist or not.

To select events on the override list,
&SNLCINP
HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE =        '$DES_USERS/rebeccachen/PZQ/hostlibs/data_sompz_override.HOSTLIB'
SNCID_LIST_FILE   = 
   '$DES_USERS/rebeccachen/PZQ/hostlibs/data_sompz_override.HOSTLIB'

where the argument is the same for HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE and SNCID_LIST_FILE. There is no need to construct a separate CID list file. To more robustly select events from an override file, I added this new feature,
      SNCID_LIST_FILE  = 'HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE'
will internally replaces HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE with its argument. Thus the HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE argument can be altered and the SNCID_LIST_FILE is automatically synced.

title: fix very subtle submit_batch_jobs feature for BBC class
body:
Within the BBC class of submit_batch_jobs, the logic of naming output dirs was as follows:

1. if there are multiple input data sets (e.g., LOWZ + DES), then the output dirs have generic names OUTPUT_BBCFIT-[datasetnumber] 
2. if there is only one data set, the output dir name is the name of the data version 

While there is no explicit bug or problem here, the problem occurs when pippin is used and there is only one data set (e.g., DES only). Pippin assumes the generic folder names with OUTPUT_BBCFIT, but for a single data set the folder name is incorrect and all stage 8 (wfit) tasks fail.

Indeed this is the classic case of "it's a feature, not a bug"

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: The fix here is rather simple: remove the the logic in bullet 2 above, and always use the same logic and OUTPUT_BBCFIT naming.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: In the process of searching this issue in the code, I noticed a feature from April 1 2025 using devel_flag=41 had never been made default. This feature allows combining 1 LOWZ data set with multiple HIGH-Z data sets (and vice-versa) to enable studies in which one of the sub-sets is exactly the same. The devel_flag=41 logic has been removed, bbc_prep_1version_match_legacy() is removed, and bbc_prep_1version_match() is now called to implement the 4.01.2025 feature.

title: BayeSN option to read magerr from text file map
body: rather than computing model mag error from internal matrices, it is safer to read a magerr map from a text file.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
genmag_BAYESN.c functions init_magerr_BAYESN() and get_magerr_BAYESN() have been updated with an option to read new "GRIDMAP" (phase, wave, magerr) from BAYESN.T21_WAVEHACK/BAYESN_MODEL_MAGERR_MAP.DAT, which was created by M.Grayling & S Thorp using the BayeSN matrices.

Follow SNANA code by tracing new global variable GRIDMAP_MAGERR_BAYESN, which is fed to a python-like utility to read a multi-dimensional GRIDMAP and perform multi-D interpolation.

For now, this option is invoked with GENMODEL_MSKOPT += 2048 to enable test mode. After more testing, this option may become default.

A monitor_magerr_BAYESN() utility prints magerr in 1000 A bins, and at three phases (-10, 0, +10), so relevant experts should begin checking on this diagnostic dump.

title: Problem Overriding REDSHIFT_CMB
body:
Hello!
I am using SNANA for LC fitting, and it's been working as expected so far, but all of a sudden it no longer seems to be reading the header override file correctly anymore, and data with known z is being fitted to the wrong z (much much different). 

Here is a a snippet of my override file
```
DOCUMENTATION:
  PURPOSE: Inject peakmjds into the data
  REF:
  - AUTHOR: Nora Sherman
  - DATE: 02.12.23
DOCUMENTATION_END:
VARNAMES: CID IAUC RA DEC PKMJD REDSHIFT_CMB REDSHIFT_CMB_ERR VPEC HOSTGAL_LOGMASS HOSTGAL_RA HOSTGAL_DEC
SN: 1378707 2021acxb 49.9027958 -27.4940333 59528 0.06365 0.00001 -10.54 11.19054828 49.9049134 -27.4965505
SN: 1370113 2021aefx 64.9721667 -54.9479444 59550 0.00473963 0.0005 -312.27 10.39459102 65.00165353 -54.93795131
```
But, after running fitting, for CID 1378707, I get a zHEL of 1.17004. Given the override REDSHIFT_CMB value of 0.06365, this seems hugely excessive! There are several examples of this as well.

The most concerning part, however, is that not long ago I was getting very normal zHEL values, but I just updated my override file, and then this started happening, so I hazard that it might be an issue with my override file, but I cannot identify what might be going wrong (it looks identical but for the updated values in the file which, I am convinced, should not result in such high zHELs). 

Any assistance is greatly appreciated. Thank you!

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
in SIMGEN_INCLUDE_SNPRECURSOR.INPUT the Gauss profile was added but "SIMSED_GRIDONLY:  PRERSG_INDEX" was not removed, resulting in conflict. Later I will fix sim to abort on these conflicting requests.

I commented out the SIMSED_GRIDONLY key, and sim aborts with
 FATAL ERROR ABORT called by interp_flux_SIMSED
   Corners[0] already filled; two data points have the same coordinates.

The problem is that the SED grid is really 5D, so giving only 1D to interpolate is ambiguous because all of the values are repeated many times, and it can't figure out which SED you want. Try defining Gauss profile in all 5 dimensions; set large sigma to get flat distribution.

title: Match error between SIM_REDSHIFT_HOST and the redshift in HOSTLIB input file
body:
Hi,

When simulating using a HOSTLIB with the redshift match option I noticed a discrepancy between the stored redshifts `SIM_REDSHIFT_HOST` and the input redshifts in the HOSTLIB.

I've setup an input file at `/project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/PS1MD/USERS/bcarreres/DEBUG_Z/SIMGEN_LOWZ_DEBUGZ.INPUT`
that result in a simulation at `/project2/rkessler/PRODUCTS/SNDATA_ROOT/SIM/DEBUG_Z/`. The DUMP file contains  the `GALID` that allow to retrieve the HOST from the HOSTLIB: `/project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/PS1MD/USERS/bcarreres/SIMLIB/PanthP_HOSTLIB.HOSTLIB`

The config for host is:
```
HOSTLIB_FILE: /project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/PS1MD/USERS/bcarreres/SIMLIB/PanthP_HOSTLIB.HOSTLIB
HOSTLIB_MSKOPT: 536 # Use Host coord (+8), adjust SN redshift (+16), and peculiar velocity (+512) 
HOSTLIB_DZTOL: 0.0001 0 0 
HOSTLIB_STOREPAR: VPEC,ZTRUE_CMB,GROUPID,UCHUUID

VEL_CMBAPEX: 0 # Cancel vel CMB
```
The DZTOL is set to 1e-4 but we can observe a discrepancy up to 1e-3.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
with your option VEL_CMBAPEX=0, there were still a few places where the CMB<->HEL translator was applied and thus inconsistent with other parts of the code. This bug-fix includes adding previously missed VEL_CMBAPEX checks in transform_ZTRUE_HOSTLIB()  and SORT_SNHOST_byDDLR(). 

Beware that since VPEC is in your HOSTLIB, but not VPECERR, VPEC is applied without fluctuation (i.e., VPECERR=0). The reported REDSHIFT_HELIO and REDSHIFT_FINAL include uncorrected VPEC, and thus differs from ZTRUE_CMB.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
To verify the original ZTRUE_CMB in the HOSTLIB, run the script
 ././MAKE_SNANA_TABLE.sh
and check zHD column printed to stdout. SNANA analysis jobs apply vPec correction to zCMB and report zHD (redshift to use with Hubble diagram). In this case with VPECERR=0, zHD is the true CMB redshift.

As a reminder, this awkward treatment of VPEC corrections is motivated by a lack of consensus model for the correction. To enable flexibility on choice of VPEC model, an arbitrary VPEC model can be used to override VPEC in the data file (see HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE in manual), and output zHD (from snana.exe or snlc_fit.exe) is updated accordingly.

comments.body: Resolved ! Thanks!

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: This job above uses NSPLITRAN, and it likely conflicts with a recent refactor to speed up the BBC preparation.

comments.author: rebeccachen0
comments.body: For what it's worth, I didn't run into the same issue here: /scratch/midway2/rkessler/PIPPIN_OUTPUT/RC_DESPZ_MASTER/6_BIASCOR/P21NOM which I also ran recently using NSPLITRAN

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
It is indeed a subtle bug with recent refactor, but it has nothing to do with NSPLITRAN. The gzipping is divide into 10 cores, but in above job only 1 core is needed and the wait-for-gzip logic didn't wait. Fix is to check wait upon reaching 10 gzip jobs, or if there are fewer than 10 gzip jobs.

I also added more robust logic to not only require a certain number of INPUT\*FITRES.gz files, but also require zero INPUT\*FITRES files so that BBC doesn't start while gzip is still going.

title: refactor kcor/calib code
body: For readiing/storing/implementing kcor/calib fits files, convert the fortran utilities into C-code (sntools_calib.h[c]). Make similar translation for host-galaxy extinction (genmag_extinction.c[h]). The goal is to translate fortran utilities into C code so that fortran (snlc_fit.exe) calls C functions, but C codes (e..g, sim, SALT2mu) do not call fortran routines. Another goal is to improve refactored code organization for long-term maintenance.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
To test kcor refactor:
snlc_sim.exe <inputFile>  USE_KCOR_REFACTOR 2
slc_fit.exe <inputFile>      USE_KCOR_REFACTOR T

The legacy & refactored code have perfect agreement for SALT2 model. For MLCS, snoopy however, the AVwarp refactor differs by ~.001 mag from original. This small difference can lead to ~.01  differences in fitted DLMAG because of the chaotic behavior of light curve fitting. Using refactored code in the regression test, 14 of 94 tests fail due to slight numerical issues with MLCS.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: Nov 28 2022, release v11_04o tag with refactored code working using USE_KCOR_REFACTOR flags. Default is still legacy, and plan to make refactored code default on Friday Dec 2 2022.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: Dec 2 2022: release refactored code as planned a few days ago.

title: Rest frame lambda bug when light-curve fitting
body:
When fitting light curves, it seems like the `RESTLAMBDA_FITRAN` key is not being read. I have an object at z~1 where the LC fitting should ignore the Roman R-band, but is causing a failure instead.

```
  PRE-ABORT DUMP from function checkLamRange_SEDMODEL :
  Calling function 'genmag_SALT2' passed ifilt=6('R062-R') and z=1.0840
  Rest-frame Lambda-Range (LAMREST_MIN/MAX)  = 1962.577037 to 3795.595199
  SED Lambda-Range: 2000.000000 to 20000.000000
  LAMFAIL_LO/HI = 1, 0
```

In the nml file, I have `RESTLAMBDA_FITRANGE = 3000. , 20000.`. You can reproduce this bug with the command can be found in `$SNANA_DEBUG/restframe_lambda_bug/`.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: above abort is a protective feature, not a bug. At z=1.08, R-band filter extends 38A bluer than the model limit of 2000 A, so the program aborts to avoid undefined flux. In RICK.nml, I set the min wavelength to 3200 A (instead of 3000) and the event above was fit without error.

comments.author: benjaminrose
comments.body:
Why would it ignore the R band with the min fit wavelength set to 3200 but try to fit the R band if the min fit wavelength is set to 3000?

Will SNANA use the band if any part of the band is within RESTLAMBDA_FITRANGE?

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
RESTLAMBDA_FITRANGE defines central wavelength of passband ... but the filter edges (blue and red) must be within the SED-model ranges, otherwise it aborts. Shifting 3000 -> 3200 results in excluding R-band as indicated by this stdout line
     FIT OBSERVER FILTERS YJZ

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: it's quite fortunate that we changed the definition of MUERR_RAW because that led to identifying another serious problem. Since MUERR_RAW no longer includes MUERR_VPEC, COV(RAW) should be >0 ... but it is negative for duplicate events!  We didn't catch this before because adding SQMUERR_VPEC was preventing sqrt(negative number). First, I fixed the code to properly trap negative COV and abort with proper error message. I strongly recommend combining duplicates at the light level before LC fits ... hacking the fix in BBC is not reliable and I have never trusted it.

title: No way to correctly specify library location in Ubuntu

I tried to install SNANA on Ubuntu 20.04 and had a problem with GSL static libraries location. comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Back in April 2026, issue https://github.com/RickKessler/SNANA/issues/1649 
changed the number of stored hosts from MXHOSTGAL = 2 -> 3. While the number of written hosts is truncated, NMATCH and NMATCH2 record total number of matches. In the DES-SN5YR DR, only 2 hosts were recorded, but SNID=1432026 has NMATCH=3. WIth current MXHOSTGAL=3, the 3rd host has all zeros, leading to log(0) somewhere in the HOST_CONFUSION (HC) computation. The fix for defining HC arguments is to define a local NMATCH2_DEFINED counter (snana.F90) that increments only if SNHOST_OBJID(igal) != 0, so that suppressed hosts are excluded from the HC calculation. This logic should be robust if MXHOSTGAL is increased in the future.

Added stdout warning:
HOST_CONFUSION WARNING: NMATCH2= 3 but only 2 HOSTS recorded for CID=1432026
but there is nothing in the output SNANA or FITRES table to indicate loss of information for HC.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
New DES-SN5YR sims will record all three hosts and thus provide a more correct HC calculation compared to the real-data DR in which only 2 of the 3 hosts go into the HC calculation. To enable a more accurate sim for NMATCH=3 events, I may add a new sim-input key
MXHOSTGAL_FORCE: 2
Unfortunately there is no clear way to automate this feature, and thus users would have to remember adding this key if the HC calculation is important.

title: `read_searcheff_raw_varnames` hardcodes `MXSUBSTR=4`, ignoring `MXSUBSTR_SEARCHEFF_MAP` — aborts on SPECEFF/zHOST maps combining >4 filters
body:
## Summary

`read_searcheff_raw_varnames` (`src/sntools_trigger.c`) hardcodes the filter-split bound to `4`, which is inconsistent with the sibling parser `assign_MAP_VARNAME_FILTERS` in the same file. Any SEARCHEFF_SPEC / SEARCHEFF_zHOST map whose `VARNAMES` combines more than 4 filters with `+`/`-` aborts, even though the map machinery itself supports up to `MXSUBSTR_SEARCHEFF_MAP` (=60).

## Abort message

```
FATAL ERROR ABORT called by read_searcheff_raw_varnames->nsplitString->splitString
  Nsplit = 8  exceeds bound MXsplit=4
  string to split= 'a+b+c+d+e+f+g+h'  ; split separator= '+'
```

## Root cause

Two parsers in `src/sntools_trigger.c` split the map `VARNAMES` on `+`/`-`, but use different bounds:

- `assign_MAP_VARNAME_FILTERS` — **correct**:
  ```c
  int MXSUBSTR = MXSUBSTR_SEARCHEFF_MAP;   // line ~1624  (=60)
  ```
- `read_searcheff_raw_varnames` — **stale literal**:
  ```c
  int MXSUBSTR=4, NSUBSTR, isub ;          // line ~1840
  ```

`read_searcheff_raw_varnames` runs first (as the raw-varname pre-reader), so it aborts before the map parser that would have accepted the same string. The header already documents the intended limit:

```c
// src/sntools_trigger.h:53
#define MXSUBSTR_SEARCHEFF_MAP 60 // e.g., g+r+i+z is max number of + separated substrings
```

Both functions were introduced in the SEARCHEFF refactor (commit `95ff5c0`, 2026-03-27); `MXSUBSTR_SEARCHEFF_MAP` was later raised from 4 → 60 (commit `a9c59b3`, 2026-05-22), but the hardcoded `4` in `read_searcheff_raw_varnames` was missed.

## Proposed fix

`src/sntools_trigger.c`, `read_searcheff_raw_varnames`:

```diff
-  int MXSUBSTR=4, NSUBSTR, isub ;
+  int MXSUBSTR = MXSUBSTR_SEARCHEFF_MAP, NSUBSTR, isub ;
```

Purely enlarges a bound (60 ≥ any realistic filter count), so it is backward-compatible and has no effect on maps combining ≤4 filters.

## How to reproduce

Run `pippin.sh -v JT_TITAN_SPECEFF.yml` from `/project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/ATLAS/USERS/jtweddle/EFFICIENCIES/PIPPIN_FILES`. Abort occurs during map read.

## Context / motivation

ATLAS has 8 (a–h) orange bands to reflect the different CCD+filter combinations across the different telescope units. A single combined-band block `a+b+c+d+e+f+g+h` is the correct way to key the spec-classification efficiency on the source's peak orange mag (the `+` path in `get_searcheff_mag` averages the valid per-chip peak mags). Splitting into 8 separate single-band blocks is not equivalent — they OR-combine and, with `OPT_EXTRAP` on the `−9` sentinels of unobserved chips, silently return eff=1. So the combined block is, I believe, required, and it currently can't be parsed.

title: new &FITINP  VARLIST_PDF to select subset of variables for marginalization
body:
If NGRID_PDF > 0 and NSIGMA_PDF > 0 ( both in &FITINP), the default marginalization is over all fitted variables. For zPHOT fit with 5 variables and NGRID_PDF = 11,  11**5 = 169,000 function evaluations can take a long time. To reduce marginalization time, a subset of relevant parameters may be adequate, e.g.,
  &FITINP
    NGRID_PDF = 11
    NSIGMA_PDF = 3
    VARLIST_PDF 'c,x0,zPHOT'  ! <== new input

performs 11**3 = 1131 function evaluations, or less than 1% compared to the default marginalization.

title: Possible bug in check_vpec_sign
body:
We are working with Maria Acevedo on PV corrections for DEBASS. And we encouter an error on the check_vpec_sign().
We are not sure of why...

Few years ago we corrected the PV implementation to be such as:
```
    IF ( DOCOR_VPEC ) THEN

       ZPEC     = ( SNLC_VPEC     / SNGL(CLIGHT) )
       ZPECERR  = ( SNLC_VPEC_ERR / SNGL(CLIGHT) )

       if ( RESTORE_WRONG_VPEC ) then
!    use incorrect VPEC convention ... to be deleted someday
          SNLC_ZHD = (1.0+SNLC_ZCMB) * (1.0+ZPEC) - 1.0  ! Jan 2018;
       else
!    use correct VPEC convention
          SNLC_ZHD = (1.0+SNLC_ZCMB) / (1.0+ZPEC) - 1.0  ! Oct 2020
       endif

       ZERR1 = SNLC_ZCMB_ERR
       ZERR2 = ZPECERR * (1.0 + SNLC_ZCMB) ! Eq A1, Davis 2012
       SNLC_ZHD_ERR = sqrt(ZERR1*ZERR1 + ZERR2*ZERR2)
    ENDIF

```
 [Here in snlc_fit.exe](https://github.com/RickKessler/SNANA/blob/d72b95db11516cd71e35da4359c2c1786bf91f1b/src/snana.F90#L17045)

When checking check_vpec_sign() in SALT2mu.c, it seems that it still uses the sum convention.
However I don't think it explains the bug. It seems that we got it with different PV corrections depending on the subsample we consider, I think it could be due to eventual outliers with bad PV estimation since the test doesn't consider PV estimation error.

Is there a way to skip this warning?

title: For SALT2mu (BBC), fix CUTWIN_SURVEY to work when some biasCor tables are missing cut variable
body:
Using SALT2mu.exe (BBC) for SN Unite, they recently tried to apply 
"CUTWIN  PROB_SCONE 0.8 1.0" while using PROB_SNNV19 for BBC. SALT2mu has a feature to allow missing PROB_SNNV19 column in low-z spec-confirmed BCOR subsets, but it aborts on missing PROB_SCONE that is defined for CUTWIN but plays no role in the BBC formalism.

There is already a SALT2muu feature
   "CUTWIN_SURVEY(DES)  PROB_SCONE 0.8 1.0" 
that should be ideal here, but it still aborts. Need to fix BBC code so that the survey-dependent variable (PROB_SCONE in this case) is not required to exist in every BCOR input table.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Fixed SALT2mu.exe to allow missing column for CUTWIN_SURVEY. However, this change allows real mistakes to go undetected, so also  added logic to
* init all CUTVAL[icut][isn] = -9999.88 # see CUTVAL_NONE parameter
* abort if any CUTVAL is found equal to CUTVAL_NONE

Thus it's OK to read an input table file missing PROB_SCONE as long as the desired DES survey is never found in this file. The table file containing DES must also have PROB_SCONE column to make the cut.

title: Unique RA/DECs
body:
I am interested in the positions of supernovae in my Pilot HLTDS simulations. I ran two different versions: one in which the RA/DECs are taken exactly from the SIMLIB, resulting in multiple SNe with identical RA/DECs; and one in which I use the SNANA key MXRADIUS_RANDOM_SHIFT: 0.01, which is supposed to randomly shift RA/DECs to within the given radius (in my case 0.01 arcsec). This shift seems arbitrary; what is a good rule of thumb for which value I should use for this key? 

My output on Midway without the shift: $PIPPIN_OUTPUT/JP_1TEMPLATE_7VISIT_115BUDGET_NOINTERLACE
My output on Midway WITH the shift: $PIPPIN_OUTPUT/JP_1TEMPLATE_7VISIT_115BUDGET_NOINTERLACE_RADEC

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
First of all, from the manual we have
   MXRADIUS_RANDOM_SHIFT: 0.01  # circle radius, degrees
so the unit is degrees, not arc seconds. 
There is no rule of thumb here since it is a rarely used feature.
Based on size of SIMLIB and area covered, you can compute the average distance between SIMLIB entries, so it would make sense to set MXRADIUS_RANDOM_SHIFT to something like half the mean separation.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: SIMLIB was missing NLIBID key and thus simulation could not determine random start locations for each core; this resulted in using the same LIBIDs (hence RA, DEC) for each core. To prevent future confusion, snlc_sim has been modified to abort if NLIBID key is missing for batch mode.

title: BAYESN wavelength range is not strict enough
body:
Recent pippin job with photometric sample using BAYESN results in LCFIT abort because Y-band at lower redshifts is not valid:

  - FATAL ERROR ABORT called by genmag_BAYESN->checkLamRange_SEDMODEL 
  - LSST-Y lambda range is outside defined SED range. 
  - Consider using &FITINP variable RESTLAMBDA_FITRANGE. 
  

(On Perlmutter, see $PIPPIN_OUTPUT/CBAYESN_ANALYSIS/2_LCFIT/FIT_DATA_LSST_LSST_SIMDATA)

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
I traced this abort to a non-SNIa event that has a broader wavelength range compared to BayeSN. The sim code protects SNIa-BAYESN, but doesn't protect non-IA because it doesn't know that BAYESN will be used later at LCFIT stage. The problem is here in the BAYESN.YAML file:

L_FILTER_CEN_MIN: 4500
L_FILTER_CEN_MAX: 8500   <=== too close to SED upper bound of 9500
L_SED_MIN: 3500
L_SED_MAX: 9500

The central wavelength limit of 8500 is too close to the max SED range of 9500, and Y-band centered at 8500 can still leak out of the SED range.

This problem would eventually fail on real data that records all bands regardless of redshift, and it indeed fails on ELASTICC SNIa that records all bands regardless of redshift or rest-frame wavelength. I setup an elastic test job here,

$PIPPIN_OUTPUT/CBAYESN_ANALYSIS/2_LCFIT/FIT_DATA_LSST_LSST_SIMDATA/output/SPLIT_JOBS_LCFIT/rick_elasticc.sh

that ABORTS rather quickly, so I would suggest tuning L_FILTER_CEN_MAX until LCFIT-BAYESN can process ELASTICC Ia without the wavelength range ABORT

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: temp solution is to artificially extend phase and wavelength range in existing BAYESN models; longer term plan is to improve training to include wider phase range.

title: Issue: wfit.exe returns w = -1 no matter what the input Hubble diagram is
body:
###  Issue: `wfit.exe` returns `w = -1` no matter what the input Hubble diagram is

I am experiencing `wfit.exe` returning `w = -1` when using dummy data to generate Hubble diagrams as part of learning how `wfit.exe` works.

All files are located in:

$SNANA_DEBUG/myc21_wfit

---

### Context

This is part of **Problem 4(e)** of the SNANA tutorial, where we test recovery of cosmological parameters  \$w$ and \$\Omega_M$.

I simulate an ideal redshift-binned Hubble diagram with:

Redshifts: 0.05, 0.15, …, 0.95
True parameters: ΩM = 0.3, ΩDE = 0.7, w = -1

---

###  Python Code Used

```python
import numpy as np
from astropy.cosmology import FlatwCDM

z_vals = np.array([0.05, 0.15, 0.25, 0.35, 0.45, 0.55, 0.65, 0.75, 0.85, 0.95])
cosmo = FlatwCDM(H0=70, Om0=0.3, w0=-1.0)  # or w0 = -2.0 for testing
mu_vals = cosmo.distmod(z_vals).value
sigma_mu = 0.1 * np.ones_like(mu_vals)

with open("myc21_my_hd.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("VARNAMES: CID zHD MU MUERR\n")
    for i, (z, mu, sig) in enumerate(zip(z_vals, mu_vals, sigma_mu)):
        cid = f"SN_{i+1:04d}"
        f.write(f"{cid} {z:.3f} {mu:.3f} {sig:.3f}\n")
```

---

### How I Run wfit:

wfit.exe myc21_my_hd.txt

--- 

### Problem

When I simulate a Hubble diagram using w = -2, the wfit.exe output still returns w = -1. This suggests that the input file may not be processed correctly, yet there is no error or warning to indicate an issue. Initially, I observed that I was consistently getting w = -1 from wfit.exe regardless of the Hubble diagram I provided. To test whether the code was responsive to input changes, I intentionally generated mock data with a clearly different w value (e.g., w = -2) — but the output remained unchanged. This silent behavior makes it difficult to diagnose formatting or content issues during exploratory testing.

--- 

### Request

Would you mind taking a look at my Hubble diagrams and output files in $SNANA_DEBUG/myc21_wfit? I’d appreciate it if you could help find the mistake on my end.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
see rick_hd.txt for correct syntax; the first column has to be a valid row key, either "SN:" or "ROW:". This format allows SNANA codes to ignore other lines such as comments or anything else. With 0.1 distance errors, the fitted cosmology errors are huge, so I reduced the distance errors to 0.01.

wfit.exe rick_hd.txt
fits for wCDM model. To fit w0waCDM,
wfit.exe rick_hd.txt -wa

To play with marginalization grid, see help with
wfit.exe | grep step

title: fix submit_batch_jobs to trap BBC fit error and post FAIL to ALL.DONE
body: Sometimes BBC fit gets crazy errors (too small or too large for distances). While BBC code reports this problem in the stdout and in the output YAML file, submit_batch_jobs (and hence pippin) do not read this error and the pipeline just carries on with this crazy output.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: Also found a bad crazy error trap in BBC/SALT2mu for BS21 dust model. Original crazy-error is based on assuming sigint ~ 0.1 mag ... but for dust model, very blue events have smaller distance error and thus BBC sometimes reports false crazy error warnings.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Inside SALT2mu.c code, min-M0err trap is scaled by average sqrt(muCOVscale) in the redshift bin, to avoid false alarms.

Previously only 1 repeat fit was allowed ... updated to allow up to two repeat fits (3 total).  End of STDOUT and YAML file include total number of fits: NFIT_EXEC. Usually NFIT_EXEC=1, but NFIT_EXEC>1 if crazy M0-errors are detected and the fit is repeated.

If there are crazy errors after SALT2mu/BBC fit, it writes
BAD_OUTPUT:  True

to output YAML file, and submit_batch_jobs reads BAD_OUTPUT and flags error and writes FAIL inside ALL.DONE --> pippin will stop.

title: snlc_fit: add option to use previous fit par as Gauss prior (for systematics)
body:
For small systematic shifts in snlc_fit (SALT light curve fit), the resulting fit parameters sometimes change a lot, which is not physical and results in a much larger MU error that deweights these events on the Hubble diagram. This effect is NOT captured in BBC. As an example, consider a photo-z fit with a systematic shift that results in adding or dropping a band w.r.t. nominal fit ... the resulting fit-par differences can be significant.

To remove these crazy systematics outliers:
1. add option to use nominal (FITOPT000) fit parameters and errors as a Gaussian prior, and 
2. write BANDS to FITRES file, and add option to force using same bands

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Here we leverage already existing &SNLCINP input 
OPT_SNCID_LIST = 1 -> (1-bit) process CIDs from external SNCID_LIST_FILE and do NOT apply cuts
OPT_SNCID_LIST = 3 -> (1+2 bits) same as above, and also use external FIT pars as initial parameter estimate

Here we add the following new option:
OPT_SNCID_LIST = 7 (1+2+4 bits) -> same as above, and use external FITPAR and ERROR as Gauss prior. Also read new BANDS column in external FITRES file, and force fitting the same bands.

We've added the output of os.stat to the logs so far, they've requested that we amend the code with the following suggestions to get some more information:

> 2. Instead of `os.stat(merge_file)` could you do `os.access(merge_file)`?

> 3. Use a shell command to print out the file. For example something like:
>

>

Could you add these to the relevant file (I think it's read_merge_file in submit_util.py, but not 100%)?

title: snlc_fit: Fix logic problems with OPT_PHOTOZ to combine quantiles and zSpec
body:
for photo-z light curve fitting with snlc_fit.exe, the intended &FITINP logic is as follows:

OPT_PHOTOZ = 6      !  2=zSpec or 4=quantiles(Cubic interp)
OPT_PHOTOZ = 10.    ! 2=zSpec or 8=quantiles(STEFFEN intern)

However, these "combine" options simply uses zSpec or zPHOT point estimate and ignore the quantiles. OPT_PHOTOZ=4 (or 8) works correctly using only quantiles, and ignoring zSpec. The problem is thus switching from quantiles to zSpec when zSpec is available.

Note that for zPHOT point estimates (ignoring quantiles), OPT_PHOTOZ=2 picks zSpec or zPHOT correctly because REDSHIFT_FINAL is the best redshift among zPHOT and zSPEC. However, selecting among zSpec and quantiles is trickier because they involve different data elements.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
The bugs in snlc_fit.car were introduced when MASK_PHOTOZ_SOURCE was introduced a few months ago. This mask is updated each event to determine what redshift source to use, rather than relying on fixed user input OPT_PHOTOZ.

Bug 1:
subroutine FITINI_ZPRIOR was implementing only a single bit of OPT_PHOTOZ; it is now fixed to check quantile bit regardless of whether other bits are set.

Bug 2:
subroutine FITPAR_PREP logic for quantiles was incorrect; see new logic using LPZ_Q

Bug 3:
subroutine FITINI_PHOTOZ was using OPT_PHOTOZ instead of MASK_PHOTOZ_SOURCE.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: In addition to these bug fixes, we also updated init_zPDF_spline to return an error_flag for invalid quantiles, rather than abort. This allows snlc_fit to reject such events (ERRFLAG_FIT=4 in SNANA table) and move on. Function dump_zPDF() is called when error_flag is set to enable visual examination of invalid quantiles.

title: Log file not being written on lcfit failure
body:
When FILTLIST_FIT is incorrect, Pippin isn't terminating because an ALL.DONE file isn't being written. 

Pippin input file that reproduces issue:

/project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/DES/USERS/dkenworthy/pippinlearning/darcytesting.yml

See issue submitted here
[dessn/Pippin#155](https://github.com/dessn/Pippin/issues/155)

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Before investigating abort, need to figure out why submit_batch jobs continued forever. By default, a failure does not trigger "kill_jobs" unless user explicitly specifies the           --kill_on_fail option. The above jobs uses the event-sync option (opt_sncid_list) that requires FITOPT000.FITRES to exist before processing FITOPT001, etc ... So when the first (FITOPT000) fit job fails, the CPU*.CMD script hangs on infinite wait. 

The fix is to internally set args.kill_on_fail = True when event-sync is selected, and to also add a supplement kill_on_fail check in the submit_batch code, in addition to the check in the CPU*.CMD scripts.

title: fix subtle NON1ASED interpolation pathology in simulation
body:
in function interp_flux_SEDMODEL() (genmag_SEDtools.c), the flux vs. logz was interpolated using a quadratic function. At very late times and high-z, the rest-frame far-UV can vary wildly vs. wavelength, and flux(logz) values such as 
   logz = 0.234700, 0.254719, 0.274738 
   flux = 2.5e+06, 1.7e+05, 1.71e+00
can result in a quadratic fit with negative undershoot that results in negative flux. To avoid negative fluxes for data challenges and image-sim overlays, the fix to avoid is simply to replace quadratic fit with linear fit.

title: YSE SALT3 simulation is not using SIMLIB redshift even with USE_SIMLIB_REDSHIFT: 1
body:
Input files, searcheff, simlib are all on perlmutter at $SNANA_LSST_USERS/gnarayan/YSE/REFAC_SIMGEN_YSE_ZTF_NOBATCH.INPUT

We compiled a version of snlc_sim.exe with a few extra print statements, and then CUTWIN check failed.
We commented out all the CUTWIN cuts in the input file and then uncommented one by one to determine that REDSHIFT cut is the issue. 
We found that output light curves have -9 for the redshift but the SIMLIB has reasonable redshifts - can verify with:
grep REDSHIFT yselc_grizXY_dr1.simlib

So unclear why snlc_sim.exe is ignoring the redshift.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
The problem is in the sim-input file and is rather subtle. Start with this grep,

grep SEARCHEFF_ REFAC_SIMGEN_YSE_ZTF_NOBATCH.INPUT 
APPLY_SEARCHEFF_OPT:  1
SEARCHEFF_PIPELINE_EFF_FILE: $SNANA_LSST_USERS/gnarayan/YSE/SEARCHEFF_PIPELINE_YSE_DR1_SNR4_grizXY.DAT
SEARCHEFF_PIPELINE_LOGIC_FILE: $SNANA_LSST_USERS/gnarayan/YSE/SEARCHEFF_PIPELINE_LOGIC_ZTF.DAT
SEARCHEFF_SPEC_FILE:  ZERO
SEARCHEFF_zHOST_FILE:  ZERO

The last two lines state that Eff(spec-confirmation) = 0 and that Eff(zHOST) = 0;  thus there is no source of measuring a redshift, resulting in redshift = -9. The easy fix is to remove the SEARCHEFF_SPEC_FILE line, or override the ZERO argument with
   snlc_sim.exe  REFAC_SIMGEN_YSE_ZTF_NOBATCH.INPUT \
          SEARCHEFF_SPEC_FILE  NONE

If there is no SEARCHEFF_SPEC_FILE key in sim-input, the default EFF(spec-confirmation) = 1.0 and all events will have accurate zSpec.

If I comment out the line:
REDCOV: griz:0.4
in $DES_ROOT/simlibs/FLUXERRMODEL_maps/FLUXERRMODEL_SIM.DAT
everything works... so it's a problem with REDCOV

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
The underlying bug is that the sim was writing the cumulative field list for each epoch, instead of the field for each epoch. For for field overlaps, when field list becomes e.g.,  C2+C3, this C2+C3 string was written as the field epoch instead of C3. The C2+C3 field was not recognized in any REDCOV map and thus returned an error scale of 1, which resulted in COV matrix elements of zero ... which is not pos definite. 

Anticipating a related bug in the future, if the FLUXERRMODEL_FILE includes error scales that are exactly 1.000, the sim code replaces 1.00 with 1.01 to avoid GSL error "matrix not pos definite".

title: Fix Log-z binning bug for SED model
body: Redshift bin at zmax was mistakenly excluded from SIMSED flux-integral grid, and thus the last redshift bin was at zmax-zbin. For z > zmax-zbin, the SED flux-integral was used at zmax-zbin rather than interpolated. The correct distance was used, so the error here is in the K-correction. As an extreme example, SLSN in PLASTICC were generated out to 3.45, but the last z-bin was stored at z=2.7. Thus events for z>2.7 were K-corrected based on z=2.7 rather than interpolated between 2.7 and 3.45. This bug affects the highest redshift bin where events are noisy, and thus it would be difficult to notice this bug in an analysis.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: Fixed bug. SIMSED binaries should be re-generated.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: Propagated fix to Cori and re-made SIMSED binaries for LSST.

title: New fieldgroup feature in BBC
body:
for bias correcctions (BCOR) in BBC,  fieldlist_biascor is often used to define "IDSAMPLE" subsets to compute independent BCOR. FIeld overlaps give priority to the first field in the list; e.g.
fieldgroup_biascor=DDF,WFD -> overlap priority uses DDF BCOR
fieldgroup_biascor=WFD,DDF -> overlap priority uses WFD BCOR

It may be useful to explicity define a separate BCOR for overlaps, rather than using the priority; however, 
fieldgroup_biascor=WFD,DDF,WFD+DDF
results in abort due to ambiguity.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
To define field-overlaps as a separate fieldgroup,
fieldgroup_biascor=WFD,DDF,|WFD+DDF|
where the vertical bars indicate an exclusive fieldgroup that allows only the field overlap, but does not allow WFD or DDF in isolation. Be careful to monitor the overlap BCOR statistics since overlap regions may be small.

title: create_covariances.py : write uncompressed npz files instead of compressed
body:
This issue is a follow-up to https://github.com/RickKessler/SNANA/issues/1605, where the wfit C code crashes when reading covtot_inv_000.npz on Perlmutter that had been recently updated to python v3.12 (was 3.11 before). Jonah noted that 'allowe_pickle' key was missing, so he wrote a hack script to read the npz file, restore the missing 'allowe_pickle'  key, and re-write the npz files; wfit works with re-written npz files. 

After more investigation, the allowe_pickle key has nothing to do with this problem, but Jonah had accidentally re-written the npz file without compression (np.savez instead of np.savez_compressed in original create_covariance code).

The implicit assumption here is that the cnpy (C-code) library can no longer handle npz compression with python v3.12, or numpy 2.2.6 that may have been recently updated as well. 

Tests on HD with ~1000 entries show that the uncompressed npz file size is only a few percent bigger than compressed files ... as long as all of the covtot entries are filled. For the NOSYS cov that has only diagonal elements, the uncompressed file is the same size as COV with all elements, in contrast to the compressed NOSYS file that is much smaller due to compression of the redundant zeros. Gzipping the uncompressed NOSYS cov file results in a much smaller file size, but it cannot be read with C code (wfit) without unzipping it.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: create_covariance has been modified with np.savez_compressed replaced with np.savez. An AI search indicates that cpny++ can handle compressed npz files, but I will postpone such an update until later if/when there is a need to compress NOSYS cov files. Another option is to add a cov_flag (= 'cov' or 'diag') to the npz file; for the latter it would write only the diagonal elements in a 1D array.

title: Fix subtle submit_batch bug in sim merge process
body:
if zero events are written from a snlc_sim.exe task (NGENLC_WRITE=0), the output README key GENTYPE_TO_NAME is blank because the relevant information is obtained from events passing trigger. For sims with very low stats, some of the SPLIT tasks have zero events and others have a few. The sim-merge process checks only the first README file (out of the N_CORE readme files) and checks for GENTYPE_TO_NAME, which can be blank if by random chance the first README has NGENLC_WRITE=0.

This is a fairly harmless feature, except when SCONE tries to read this sim-readme key and finds insufficient information, resulting in a crash.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Two fixes have been implemented.
1. a less robust fix in snlc_sim.c to generate GENTYPE_TO_NAME information after events are generated, rather than after passing trigger. However, if an event is not generated (e.g., MJD range has no overlap with SIMLIB cadence), this fix still results in blank GENTYPE_TO_NAME in the README file


2. a more robust fix in submit_prog_sim.py to loop thru the set of README files (instead of using only the first one), and picking the first README with NGENLC_WRITE > 0.

For debugging purposes, it would be helpful to be able to bypass the crazyFlux error when simulating light curves:
```
xxx

   `|```````|`    
   <| o\ /o |>    
    | ' ; ' |     
    |  ___  |     ABORT program on Fatal Error. 
    | |' '| |     
    | `---' |     
    \_______/    

 FATAL ERROR ABORT called by check_crazyFlux
```
Because it might be useful to see the whole light curve (including crazyfluxes) to find out what is going wrong.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
snlc_sim.exe | grep SKIP
SKIP_CHECK_CRAZYFLUX: 0 # set to 1 to skip crazycheck/abort (for debug only)

body:

Thanks!

FATAL ERROR ABORT called by init_CIDRAN

title: HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE not finding match for .FITS files
body:
I am attempting to use the HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE flag to override the HOSTGAL_LOGMASS values.

For data files that use .FITS (for Unite: DES-SN5YR_DES/DES-SN5YR_LOWZ/DES-SN5YR_Foundation), the lcfit fails with:
```
  ABORT_MESSAGES: 
  - FATAL ERROR ABORT called by RD_OVERRIDE_FETCH 
  - No OVERRIDE variables are used. 
  - Make sure at least one override var matches varname in data file.
```

However for the Pantheon+ surveys, the HEADER_OVERRIDE_FILE flag works and the HOSTGAL_LOGMASS values are overridden. I have tried both HOSTGAL_LOGMASS & HOST_LOGMASS for the header in my override file based on a previous issue. Both fail.

For a working directory for this issue:
`$Unite/PIPPIN_OUTPUT/UNITE_ANALYSIS_TEST_OVERRIDE`

FAIL_SUMMARY.LOG:
`$Unite/PIPPIN_OUTPUT/UNITE_ANALYSIS_TEST_OVERRIDE/2_LCFIT/Fsys_DATAFOUND/output/FAIL_SUMMARY.LOG`

and
`$Unite = /project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/DES/USERS/ryancamo/RyanCamosRepo/midway/PPDES/Unite`

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
First, need to require HOSTGAL_LOGMASS that is in the data files (not HOST_LOGMASS). This is a strange bug in which global RD_OVERRIDE.NVAR_USE is incremented on first event, indicating that HOSTGAL_LOGMASS has indeed been found. But next event this global NVAR_USE has been mysteriously set to zero, resulting in abort. 

In sntools_data.c,  I noticed that the first two VARNAMES processed have CID='' because SNID had not been parsed yet, so I added requirement of strlen(CID)>0 to process each variable ... and this fixed the bug! I worry that this bug is related to memory overwrite, so I ran valgrind debugger as a check and there were no errors flagged. I don't know why this code change fixed the problem, so BEWARE that this bug may come back to haunt us later.

title: BBC: fix CCprior bug causing mubias=0
body: In BBC/SALT2mu.exe code, CCprior events (from simulated non-SNIa) should be bias-corrected like real data, but a bug caused mubias=0. Fortunately the invalid biasCor criteria was correctly applied to reject CCprior events.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
The fix can be implemented with BBC input
restore_des5yr=0 
The temporary default is restore_des5yr=1 to preserve the bug until Dovekie-DES cosmology submission. The DES distance changes are sub-millimag, so no harm in keeping the bug  a little longer.

title: add z-dependent rate scale option
body:
To test sensitivity to different z-dependent rate assumptions in the sim, it is much faster to pre-scale events at BBC stage to avoid re-simulation and re-doing light curve fits. Therefore, add new BBC input
   zrate_scale_file=<file>

with 2-columns (z and scale) and internally interpolate scale for each sim-data event and each sim-biascor event (Ia only in both cases). Beware that scale must be <=1 since BBC can reject events, but cannot add events.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: See new SALT2mu key  zrate_scale_file=<file>

comments.author: RickKessler

While HOST_LOGMASS appears in the output FITRES table, the correct data variables in the FITS data file is HOSTGAL_LOGMASS ... hence the override file didn't match anything in the data. I updated snana to abort if there are no matches, so now you should get

   No OVERRIDE variables are used.

To see which override variables match, grep the stdout log file as follows:

grep override <logfile>  | grep Found
	 Found override for HOSTGAL_LOGMASS

body:
I am running run_simgen_test.sh on Midway (/project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/ROMAN/USERS/rkessler/HLTDS_SIMLIB). I modified the script to use the NGEN_SEASON key (I set it to 1). I receive an error saying: "FATAL ERROR ABORT called by init_DNDZ_Rate. Cannot have both NGENTOT_LC>0 and NGEN_SEASON>0".

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
There are a few issues::
1. missing backslash after NEWMJD_DIF line
2. since NGENTOT_LC is set in SIMGEN_TRANSIENT_SNIa-normal.INPUT, is must be explicitly set to zero in the run_simgen script
3. When I finally got it running, it tried to generate 60 million events, which is way too many. I noticed this line in the SIMLIB file:
   SOLID_ANGLE: 24.605

which I suspect is in degrees^2, but should be in steridians, so multiply by 4*PI/41,000

title: Inconsistencies between flux scatter and error bars in simulated data
body:
Hi Rick,

I am experiencing some inconsistencies with scatter in my simulated data that I am finding difficult to explain.

I have calibrated my simulations such that the simulated flux errors and SNR very closely match the data, as you can see from the below plots.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d34e507-b6bc-46ec-8ac9-34999725beda)
Ratio of simulated to real flux errors as function of real AB magnitude

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/365738cf-5589-46f7-bd72-c8f5ca95f6d5)
Ratio of simulated to real SNR as function of real SNR

Given that the flux errors align, I would expect that the simulated scatter would align with the data as well. However when I look at the flux pull (defined as ```(flux-weighted_mean_flux)/flux_err``` where the weighted mean flux is computed intranight, which for ATLAS typically contains 4 exposures), I find that this is centred at zero with a standard deviation of 0.9, rather than the expected standard deviation of 1 as we see for the data (see below).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d39b9126-90ff-4357-8093-ff91322d2c40)
Flux pull distribution of simulated data

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bef5ee6-17c1-40c9-a656-6d31accbf838)
Flux pull distribution for real data

Is there something that SNANA is doing internally to alter the scatter by ~10% without altering the flux uncertainties? I see something along these lines in §4.14 of the manual, but given that I am not supplying any sort of flux error map/model I suppose this would only occur if a default map is applied in the absence of one being specified?

The sim input file I am using is located at `/project2/rkessler/SURVEYS/ATLAS/USERS/jtweddle/EFFICIENCIES/CALIBRATE/sim_input_atlas.input`, in case there is something in there that I am not using correctly.

Thanks again for your help!
Jack

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: getting the pull right to within 10% is pretty good. My guess is that the PSF characterization may not quite match, so fudging the PSF by 5% should give better agreement. Are ATLAS fluxes based on PSF photometry or aperture photometry ? And I vaguely recall that ATLAS PSF is quite large, so the images are undersampled.

title: Create Covariance failing with no MUERR_RENORM

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
I introduced a nasty memory leak in a refactor last week; should be fixed now.
The original issue (last week) was that FITS files were closed before opening next FITS file ... which meant that last FITS file was never closed. This works fine if only one data version is processed, but causes a crash if multiple data versions are processed. The recent refactor is to ensure that last FITS file is always closed. The tricky part is that last event is not necessarily read for batch jobs because only 1 of NCORE events are read, so figuring out when to close a FITS file is not so obvious. 

Today's fix keeps old logic of closing FITS file just before opening a new file ... and new logic that closes last FITS file when VERSION-DONE flag is passed after reading entire data version.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
if you output the SNANA table using
&SNLCINP
    SNTABLE_LIST = 'SNANA(text:key) FITRES'

you can examine ERRFLAG_FIT to see why events failed fit stage. In short, every event is written to the SNANA table, regardless of whether it is accepted. The ERRFLAG values are a bit cryptic and require grepping  the source code,

grep  ERRFLAG_   $SNANA_DIR/src/snlc_fit.car | grep '&' | grep =
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FITPREP_NOFILTERS  =  1  ! no valid filters
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FITPREP_NOEPOCHS   =  2  ! no epochs in FITINI_COV
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FITPREP_NEPOCH     =  3  ! too few epochs
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FITPREP_QUANTILES  =  4  ! quantiles either negative or not increasing
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FITPREP_ADJUST     =  5  ! bad chi2 on initial params (July 2024)
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FIT_BADCOV         =  9  ! MNSTAT returns ISTAT<3
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FIT_CRAZYERR       = 10  ! insane error detected
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FIT_MARGINALIZE    = 11  ! could not marginalize
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FIT_CUTS           = 12  ! failed 1 or more cuts
     &  ,ERRFLAG_ZFIT_DROPFILTCUTS  = 13  ! fail Zphot-cuts after drop filter
     &  ,ERRFLAG_ZFIT_RANGE         = 14  ! Zphot outside valid range
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FIT_FITPROB_ITER1  = 15  ! 1st iteration FITPROB cut (4/2024)
     &  ,ERRFLAG_FIT_SHAPE_ITER1    = 16  ! 1st iteration SHAPE cut (7/2024)

title: submit_batch_jobs.sh: need option to run multiple codes from old snana versions
body: SIM, LCFIT, BBC classes in submit_batch_jobs enable repeating with multiple sets of inputs & command-line overrides. However, only a single JOBNAME can be specified, and thus testing over previous code versions requires a separate submit-input file per code version. Need a feature to enable repeating with different code versions.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Each class now allows using the GENOPT/FITOPT/MUOPT feature to specify JOBNAME  [full path of executable]. 

The LCFIT MERGE process crashes on codes before Feb 2024 because one of the YAML-output key names changes (NEVT_SNANA_CUTS -> NEVT_LC_CUTS to accommodate BayeSN); a hack will be needed to process older snlc_fit.exe  codes. Older BBC code versions may crash on newly-created FITRES files that can have much longer text lines to parse that exceed allocated string memory in older codes.

========================================
For sim the submit_batch inputs looks like:

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
The main issue is that there is no sim-input file (above) and thus snlc_sim interprets the SIMLIB file as a sim input file, and the abort is thus correct.

To simplify implementation of SIMLIB_DUMP, there are two code updates:

1) sim-input file need contain only the SIMLIB_FILE keys other required keys (GENMODEL, KCOR_FILE, GENFILTERS) are not needed

2) replacing sim-input file with NOFILE, a command-line only argument can be used for the dump ; e.g.
  snlc_sim.exe NOFILE   SIMLIB_FILE $SNANA_LSST_ROOT/simlibs/LSST_DC2_Run2.2i_WFD.SIMLIB \. SIMLIB_DUMP 1

The SIMLIB_DUMP section of the SNANA manual has been updated accordingly.

         NONZERO_SEARCHEFF_zHOST=1

    \_______/

 FATAL ERROR ABORT called by check_APPLYMASK_SEARCHEFF
   Invalid user-input 'APPLY_SEARCHEFF_OPT: 5' (OVP=1)
   Simulation can produce SEARCHEFF mask 3`

SEARCHEFF_zHOST_FILE is specified, so not sure why APPLY_SEARCHEFF_OPT: 5 is not valid?

Error can be reproduced with: `/scratch/midway2/rkessler/PIPPIN_OUTPUT/RC_ROMAN/1_SIM/ROMAN_BS20_mass/LOGS/FAIL_REPEAT_PIP_RC_ROMAN_ROMAN_BS20_mass_SNIaMODEL0-0001_53210.CMD`

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
This abort is due to a very old default in which EFF(spec) = 1.0 if the user does not specify a spec-Eff map file. Since you did not specify EFF(spec) map, the 100% spec-confirmed sample means that there are no zPHOT events, and thus APPLY_SEARCHEFF_MASK=5 is not possible. The simple fix is to add this into your sim-input file or command line arguments:
   SEARCHEFF_SPEC_FILE:   ZERO 

By explicitly setting EFf(spec) = 0, the zPHOT sample is well defined.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
This is a very odd case involving two subtle bugs. First, there is an old option to use host photo-z for every event with
   GENSIGMA_REDSHIFT:  1.0
The first bug is that this option sets both REDSHIFT_HELIO and REDSHIFT_CMB equal to ZPHOT_HOST, which can fail the zTOL (zHEL<->zCMB) test in snlc_fit.exe.

However, this bug is not what caused the above abort because the above sim-input has "GENSIGMA_REDSHIFT: 0" and uses zHOST efficiency map to determine which subset of events has zPHOT (instead of zSPEC). The above event selected a very rare galaxy that has zPHOTERR = 1.06 (> 1.0). This triggered the 2nd bug in which the actual zERR > 1 was used as a flag to set REDSFHIT_HELIO = REDSHIFT_CMB = zPHOT_HOST, instead of checking the user input GENSIGMA_REDSHIFT.

Both bugs have been fixed.

To avoid the zTOL abort when running snana.exe/snlc_fit.exe on old sims with the above-mentioned bugs, the zTOL test is skipped when SNLC_ZHELIO_ERROR >. 1.0.
