title: Change MXSTORE_RAN in simulation to avoid repeat random sequences using submit_batch_jobs
body:
While chasing a very subtle bias in the analyzed average of 50 simulated LSST samples, I noticed duplicates in the biasCor sample. The SNIDs are all unique, but SIM_[z,c,x1,a,b] all matched exactly for several events. To diagnose this further, I added this feature to BBC:
   SALT2mu.exe <inputFile>  check_duplicates_biascor=1
which exits after running the check. This check-option works only on command line (interactively) to avoid consuming extra memory in slurm. 

While the data-duplicate check is based on SNID, the biasCor check is based on redshift, color, stretch. For the biasCor sample of 2.8 million events, only 478,000 were unique. The number of duplicates ranges from a few up to 20. In short, the effective size of the biasCor sample here is only about 1/6 of what we wanted.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
The underlying problem is rather subtle and seems to be a bit of bad luck picking numbers. First recall how unique SNIDs are chosen among independent sim-jobs running on separate cores. Each sim task has its own JOBID that it uses to re-generate all of the previous random SNIDs (for lower numbered JOBIDs), store them on a list, and then pick new SNIDs that don't overlap the list. The number of randoms stored per event is 3000 (3 lists, 1000 per list), and thus if the number of pre-computed randoms is a multiple of 3000, there will be exact random-sequence overlap between two sim tasks.

The bad luck part was selecting NGENTOT_LC that is a multiple of 1000, and submit_batch adds 1000 to number of generated randoms (NRANGEN) as a safety margin. These multiples of 1000 lead to many sim-tasks pre-computing NRANGEN randoms that is a multiple of 3000.

If we had used NGEN_UNIT, which multiplies a physical rate, the number of events would likely not be a multiple of 1000, thus avoiding the problem.

To greatly reduce such bad-luck numbers, two fixes have been made:
1) MXSTORE_RAN in sim is changed from 1000 to 1001,
2) submit_batch NRANGEN safety margin -> 1013 (instead of 1000)

This seemingly small change breaks the random sequence from previous code versions, and thus about half of the regression tests fail. Some of the SIMFIT fail due to SNID no longer existing in the sim-output. With this change, a new tag must be created ASAP along with a new reference for regression testing.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
in a recent update to avoid slow Cholesky deconp, 
   https://github.com/RickKessler/SNANA/issues/1195
the current crash is because NOBS=0 (after SNR>2 cut) passes a zero-size matrix to Cholesky decomposition. The fix is to skip the decomposition in this case.

As an aside, see fixed SIMGEN_DUMP argument.

title: Need utility to extract spectra into format suitable for astrodash
body: Astrodash ,SNID, etc ... cannot read spectra from SNANA-formatted data files, so need an extraction utility.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Provided a 2-step solution that works for both real data and sim.
First, can run the base snana.exe program as follows:
   snana.exe  NOFILE VERSION_PHOTOMETRY <version> OPT_REFORMAT_SPECTRA 1
to extract each spectrum into a separate file with 3 columns: lam Flam Flamerr.

A higher level utility has been added to quick_commands, e.g.,    
   quick_commands.py \ 
      --extract_spectra_format astrodash 
     -v $SNDATA_ROOT/lcmerge/SALT3TRAIN_K21-Frag/SAL\*

will extract spectra from all of the SALT3TRAIN_K21-Frag data files using the wildcard. 

NOTES:
* this formalism allows other formats to be easily added. 
* both snana.exe and quick_commands.py write spectral text files in cwd (i.e., an output folder is NOT created)
* Beware that current text format of one-spectrum-per-file is inefficient for large samples.

title: BBC INPUT_FITOPT000.FITRES: both gzipped and unzipped files created
body:
Hello,
somehting is not properly working in BBC.
For some reason, INPUT_FITOPT000.FITRES are correctly created but some are tarred, some are untarred and some are duplicates.

As a result, BBC crashed with the error.
```
  - FATAL ERROR ABORT called by open_TEXTgz
  - Found gzipped and unzipped file.
  - Cannot open both files.

``` 
You can reproduce the error looking at folder: `/scratch/midway2/rkessler/PIPPIN_OUTPUT/MV-ROMAN_TRANS/6_BIASCOR/BBCRH_noLOWZsys/output_ITER1`

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Recently, the gzipping of INPUT_FITOPT*.FITRES files was modified to gzip more quickly by doing parallel gzip with groups of 10 files. The problem above is that the number of files per group is 10 10 10 10 4 ... and the only the last gzip command did NOT have ampersand to force waiting before returning control to submit_batch. Gzipping 4 files is quicker than gzipping 10 files, and thus submit_batch moved on before all files were gzipped.

Two fixes were made. First, the gzip file groups are submitted in reverse order so that the group with missing ampersand (wait for gzip to finish) always has 10 files. Second, after control is returned to submit_batch, it counts the number of existing .gz files and doesn't return until the expected number of .gz files exists.

title: SED mag smear bug fix in genmag_PySEDMODEL
body: For simulating spectra with PySEDMODEL, back in Dec 2020, a local magSmear array was replaced with a global GENSMEAR.MAGSMEAR_LIST array. This array implements intrinsic scatter models such as G10 or C11. The global array was computed, but the local array, whose values were no longer set, was used to modify the true SED fluxes. The unset magSmear values are most likely zero, but they can take on arbitrary/crazy values depending on compiler options and platform.

title: Better handling of `Invalid muErrsq` errors
body:
When working with large bias sims, you will sometimes produces supernovae with large `muErrsq` values, especially when working with the C11 intrinsic scatter model.

This will then produce an error in the BIASCOR stage in `output_ITER1/FAIL_SUMMARY.LOG` similar to the following:
```
FAILURE-0001:
  JOB_LOG_FILE:       OUTPUT_BBCFIT_FITOPT000_MUOPT001.LOG
  FAIL_REPEAT_SCRIPT: FAIL_REPEAT_OUTPUT_BBCFIT_FITOPT000_MUOPT001.CMD
  FAIL_MODE:          ABORT
  ABORT_MESSAGES:
  - FATAL ERROR ABORT called by makeMap_sigmu_biasCor
  - Invalid muErrsq=106.055891 for ievt=617323 (SNID=8257957)
  - Something is messed up.
```
This in turn produces an error in `output/FAIL_SUMMARY.LOG` similar to:
```
FAILURE-0001:
  JOB_LOG_FILE:       OUTPUT_BBCFIT_FITOPT000_MUOPT002.LOG
  FAIL_REPEAT_SCRIPT: FAIL_REPEAT_OUTPUT_BBCFIT_FITOPT000_MUOPT002.CMD
  FAIL_MODE:          ABORT
  ABORT_MESSAGES:
  - FATAL ERROR ABORT called by match_cidlist_init
  - CID TABLE DOES NOT EXIST
  - Check file /scratch/midway2/rkessler/PIPPIN_OUTPUT/PA_D5YR_SIM/6_BIASCOR/P21NOM_SIGINT_COLOR/output_ITER1/OUTPUT_BBCFIT/BBC_ACCEPT_SUMMARY.LIST
```

The solution at the moment is to go to the `MERGE` output, find the `FITOPT*.gz` file containing the offending `SNID`, delete that line, and run BBC again. This process will sometimes need to be repeated twice or thrice, taking up a lot of time.

I propose that if a supernova is found with an Invalid muErrsq, it is simply ignored and added to a list of invalid supernovae. This list can then be reported as a warning for further investigation. If this list becomes very large (say, 1% of the total number of supernovae) then it would be reasonable to crash, but at that point you'd know every supernovae with an invalid muErrsq, not just one.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
We had a similar problem using a very large biasCor for SNIa-photoz study. After isolating the event, it clearly had a crazy color uncertainty that we removed at LCFIT stage with
&FITINP
    FITWIN_COLOR_ERR = 0.0, 1.0     ! cut on c_err

Can you isolate the event causing muErrsq=106.055891 and extract the SALT2 fitted parameters and errors ... then compare to a plot of the entire distribution and hopefully there is a safe outlier cut.

In short, while such SALT2mu aborts are annoying, I think it is better to know what's going on and fix it upstream, rather than hiding the issue.

comments.body:
The lack of error message was because stdout was piped with > MERGE*LOG instead of &> MERGE*.LOG. Submit_batch is fixed so that future error messages should appear in the MERGE LOGS.

The underlying cause of the merge error is that 1 of the 70 split jobs was missing the HOST_SBMAG_[band] columns. These columns are created after reading the first event if HOST_SBMAG are defined ... but by bad luck, the first real-data event for this split task has undefined SBMAG, likely due to a problem with the template forced photometry. Since the HOST mags were ok, the table-creation logic has been changed to require either SBMAG or HOST_MAGs to exist.

title: Update SIM to abort on repeat KEY in an INCLUDE file
body:
A long time ago the sim-input reader was updated to abort on duplicate keys in the input file while allowing command-line overrides. However, the implementation works only for keys in the same file ... a duplicate key in the primary input and INCLUDE file does not trigger abort. Allowing duplicate keys in separate files is risky because there is no obvious hierarchy and can lead to mistakes if a change is made in only one of the files. 

Plan is to implement this abort-check as originally intended: abort on duplicates regardless of input file or include file. However, an INCLUDE file passed via command line is treated like any other command-line override and will not cause abort. This update may cause some aborts and perhaps find a few input key mistakes.

title: SALT2 training features
body:
It seems that the submit_batch_jobs.sh implementation of SALT2 training is the most user-friendly way of training on Midway, but there's currently no way to train an unperturbed surface  (i.e. if you don't specify a TRAINOPT perturbation, the script won't compile). The script automatically trains an unperturbed surface alongside any TRAINOPTS specified, could we add an option to train this unperturbed surface without requiring TRAINOPTS?

Along the same line, the training sample is currently specified "under the hood" (in $PRODUCTS/snpca/train_SALT2.py) as 'trainingsample_snls_sdss_v5.list' in the base folder (PATH_INPUT_CALIB in the submit_batch input script). To change the training sample used, I need to copy the entire base folder and edit the training sample list, without changing the name. Can we add a feature to specify the full path of the training sample, rather than taking it from PATH_INPUT_CALIB? I can make any changes to the train_SALT2.py script if needed.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body: GT added TRAINOPT_GLOBAL feature.

title: MXEPSIM_PERFILT limit hit with high-cadence IDEAL sims
body:
I am running a set of sims with very high cadence (0.1 day sampling) IDEAL sims for @fedhere for her cadence studies. The plan is to interpolate these IDEAL light curves and then resampling them onto any arbitrary LSST cadence for use with the metrics analysis framework.

The simlib for these high cadence IDEAL sims is on cori at 
`$SNANA_LSST_ROOT/simlibs/LSST_IDEAL_0.1DAY_LONG.SIMLIB`

The short version of the same SIMLIB (same MJD start and step, much smaller range - similar filename without _LONG) works fine, but when I launch the sim with the long (~150 day) SIMLIB I see this error: 

```
 FATAL ERROR ABORT called by NEPFILT_GENLC
   NEP=1000 exceeds bound for ifilt_obs=1(u).
   Check MXEPSIM_PERFILT
```   

which I think is related to the number of epochs in each filter. 

While I agree that 150 days at 0.1 day sampling will generate a lot of observations, I'm also keen to accommodate this request since it impacts the LSST Cadence Discussions. Is there some way we can increase the limit? Or if not is there a way to use a different SIMLIB per model? This way fast-evolving transients and variables can use the 0.1-day SIMLIB, while slower evolving sources can use a lower cadence SIMLIB.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
this was a really evil bug. There is a check on whether SNHOST_SB__FLUXCAL exists that determines if it goes into the output tables. However, I had mistakenly made the check assuming mag (SBFLUX < 99 ==> exists) instead of FLUXCAL. In rare cases, the first event has a really bright SB where all bands have SB_FLUXCAL > 99, so the code incorrectly sets the EXIST flag to false and excludes HOST_SB from output table. If all ROOT tables but one have SB_FLUXCAL columns, the merge process fails.

It's fixed.

Currently, in the SALT2 training with submit_batch_jobs, CfA3 maps to Standard, Keplercam, and 4Shooter2 instrument files, so all three are perturbed with a call to CfA3.  It'd be good to be able to perturb each instrument individually. I think that all we need to do is add some entries to survey.yaml to specify different instruments, i.e. by adding the following:

```
CfA3_4SHOOTER2:
    MagSys: VEGA2
    MagSys_filename: BD17-jla1.dat
    Instrument: [ 4SHOOTER2 ]
    Instrument_subdir: [ 4Shooter2 ]
    Bands: [ Us, B, V, R, I ]
    SNANA_INSTR:  [ CFA3S ]
    SNANA_BANDS:  [ s, B, V, R, I ] ??q

CfA3_STANDARD:
    MagSys: VEGA2
    MagSys_filename: BD17-jla1.dat
    Instrument: [ STANDARD]
    Instrument_subdir: [ SNLS3-Landolt-model ]
    Bands: [ U, B, V, R, I ]
    SNANA_INSTR:  [ CFA3 ]
    SNANA_BANDS:  [ U, B, V, R, I ]

CfA3_KEPLERCAM:
    MagSys: VEGA2
    MagSys_filename: BD17-jla1.dat
    Instrument: [ KEPLERCAM ]
    Instrument_subdir: [ Keplercam ]
    Bands: [ Us, B, V, r, I ]
    SNANA_INSTR:  [ CFA3K ]
    SNANA_BANDS:  [ s, B, V, r, i ]
```

I can do this, but I need a few things confirmed:
- The SURVEY_MAP_FILE for submit_batch_jobs currently points to the survey.yaml file in the T20 SALTPATH in my user directory. Are we happy with keeping it there, or could we point it to the copy in $PRODUCTS/snpca instead?
- Do we want to keep a 'CfA3' option that perturbs all three instruments? If so, there should maybe be a warning message that a call to this survey will perturb multiple instruments at once.
- Are the SNANA_INSTR and BANDS I've included above correct, and are you happy with the CfA3_INSTRUMENT formatting, or is there something else that makes more sense?
- I noticed that SNANA_INSTR and SNANA_BANDS sections are missing for Calan/Tololo and Other, is that intentional/fine?

Once I get the go-ahead on this, I'll update survey.yaml and do some tests.

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
Fixed subtle numerical artifact in function merge_duplicate(). Nominal merged COV for duplicates is given by
    COV_merge = [ sum 1/cov_orig ]^-1 
which is inspired by the weighted average formula:  1/sigma^2 = sum[1/sigma_i^2]. For 2009D above, the COV(x1,c) element has opposite sign for the two duplicates, and the resulting sum is very close to zero, but slightly negative. This leads to a large negative COV_merge(x1,c) element, causing MUERRSQ < 0. The fix/hack is that whenever an off-diagonal element has a sign flip among the duplicates, COV_merge is the average, not the inverse-square sum above. Note that this artifact may have been present in previous analyses, but a large positive covariance could have been easily missed.

title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Allow different columns in the FITRES files passed to SALT2mu

title: NSPLITRAN option crashes BBC
body:
Adding NSPLITRAN option causes a (seemingly) unrelated crash. Relevant command is:

`SALT2mu_fit.pl $WFIRST_ROOT/SALT3/examples/wfirst/pipeline/WFIRST_BBC.input NSPLITRAN 10`

comments.author: RickKessler
comments.body:
The error is 
 FATAL ERROR ABORT : 
	 Unable to find argument of 
	 file=SALT2mu_SHALLOW+MEDIUM+DEEP/DMS/FITOPT000.FITRES
 
so you need to be in the same directory as the input FITRES  file, or provide full path of in input file. Note that INPDIR keys are ignored for NSPLITRAN, so it uses file= argument.
Please note the comments at top of SALT2mu_fit.pl:
# NSPLITRAN=<n> argument operates on the native file=<file> argument 
# in the SALT2mu-input file, and ignores the supplmental batch keys 
# INPDIR, INPDIR+,  and MUOPT. Batch keys NODELIST, BATCH_INFO and 
# SNANA_LOGIN_SETUP are used. If NSPLITRAN=<n> appears inside the 
# SALT2mu-input file, this is equivalent to the command-line specifier; 
# command-line NSPLITRAN=<n> overrides value in SALT2mu-input file. 
# The NSPLITRAN mode creates an output sub-directory with a specific 
# name, "OUT_SALT2mu_NSPLITRAN[n]", and can be changed using the 
# "OUTDIR_OVERRIDE: <OUTDIR>"  key. The output file names are hard-wired 
# with prefix=OUT_TEST. Note that for <n> split jobs, <n+1> batch jobs
# are submitted because the n+1'th job reads back all of the previous
# output and prepares a summary of averages and RMS in OUT_TEST_summary.out.
#
